newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Colombia seeks unified Latin stance against drugs.
newsitem.headline: Colombia seeks unified Latin stance against drugs.

text.p: Colombia has begun seeking a unified Latin American stance in negotiations with the United States over the drugs war, Colombia's vice minister for justice said on Tuesday.

Carlos Alberto Malagon said after talks with Brazilian officials in Brasilia that it was necessary for Latin American countries to agree on their own criteria before discussing counter narcotics cooperation with Washington.
"It's necessary that before starting talks with Washington, Latin America agrees on a unified criteria for the battle against the narcotics trade," Malagon told reporters.

Relations between Colombia, regarded as one of the world's main cocaine producers, and the United States have sunk into deep-freeze since Washington accused Colombian President Ernest Samper of using cartel money to fund his election campaign.

Colombian officials have billed the vice minister's visit to Brazil as part of Bogota's drive to "multi-lateralize" the drugs problem, saying Bolivia, Brazil, Venezuela, Peru and Ecuador are also affected by the trade.
Brazil's drug enforcement ties with the United States have also taken a beating this month after Brasilia rejected as "laughable" a $710,000 offer of anti-drugs aid from Washington.

Brazilian and Colombian officials have said they hoped to sign a cooperation accord to combat drug smuggling on their shared 990-mile (1,600-km) border, but the two countries failed to reach a formal agreement in two days of talks.
Malagon, who held talks with the number two in Brazil's Justice Ministry, Milton Seligmann, said he hoped some kind of deal would be signed in Bogota at another meeting in late November.
